clue.text: Plant nibbled by small owlet

indicators.note: the plant is a small bite taken out of the middle of the two words that follow, so its letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A garden plant has been chewed by a little young owl.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallow is a flowering herb, the family that includes the hollyhock and marshmallow.

clue.text: Driving car, doctor has to make phone call

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
taken as written
to give someone a ring is to phone them

explanation.surface: While out at the wheel, a doctor needs to stop and ring someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'make' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoring is travelling by road at the wheel of an automobile.

clue.text: Play to review when worked up?

parts.note: to review the past is to cast the mind back over it
worked up means furious, in a rage

explanation.surface: A theatre critic asks whether to write a review while still agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: John Osborne's 1956 drama gave Britain the 'angry young man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names John Osborne's landmark 1956 stage drama.

clue.text: Is introduced by newspaper editor as arranged

indicators.note: the word Is is brought in between the newspaper and the editor, placed inside their run of letters

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group, such as a party newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is brought in by the paper's editor, all neatly planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged has been put in order, planned and set out tidily.

clue.text: Scored without getting excited?

explanation.surface: A musician writes a score while staying perfectly calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is composed when its music is written; a person is composed when calm and collected.

clue.text: Water nymph provided aid once at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sea spirit once gave help to someone in the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Oceanids were the daughters of Oceanus, spirits of seas and springs.

clue.text: Old man consumes endless Italian wine and food

indicators.note: the father swallows the wine, so the wine goes inside him

parts.note: the old man is a familiar name for a father, PA

indicators.note: the wine loses its last letter

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy

explanation.surface: A father drinks Italian wine and eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the wine's last letter, and 'consumes' puts what is left inside the father; Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and the like are Italian dough products eaten as a staple meal.

clue.text: Fashion designer N disconcerted by cat enters calmly

indicators.note: something disconcerted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion designer is unsettled when a cat strolls coolly into the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted by' looks like a feeling, but it signals the shuffle of the following three words; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The British couturier, daughter of Paul, founded her own label in 2001.

clue.text: Dance move one's taken up during parties

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits in the middle of the parties

parts.note: a do is a party, so two of them are DO DO

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I'S, here written as IS

explanation.surface: A dance step is picked up by a guest at a round of parties.
explanation.definitionFit: In square and country dancing, partners pass round each other back to back.

clue.text: Workforce on a N A Scottish island

parts.note: the staff are the people working for an organisation

explanation.surface: Employees are posted to a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffa is the small Hebridean isle off Mull, home of Fingal's Cave; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an uninhabited isle of the Inner Hebrides famous for basalt columns.

clue.text: Such lack of consideration unlikely among philosophers

definitions.text: Such lack of consideration unlikely among philosophers

parts.words: Such lack of consideration unlikely among philosophers
parts.note: philosophers are all about reflection, so a state of being without reflection is the last thing found among them; the word itself splits as a lack of thought

explanation.surface: Philosophers are rarely accused of being inconsiderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inconsiderate and careless of others' feelings is a want of reflection.

clue.text: Wrongly take in Christmas visitor?

parts.note: to rob is to take something unlawfully
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a guest at Christmas by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The red-breasted bird appears on British Christmas cards and visits gardens in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted songbird is a traditional Christmas card visitor to the garden.

clue.text: Like some birds pursued by admirer

parts.note: a fan is a devoted admirer
to tail someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Birds are followed by a keen enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursued by admirer' reads as a chase, but the admirer comes first and the pursuit follows; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain pigeons and flycatchers have tail feathers that spread out in a wide arc.

clue.text: Capital one invested in failing casino

indicators.note: money invested in a business is put inside it, so the one goes in
a failing business is collapsing, so its letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Somebody puts money into a struggling gambling house.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the chief city and seat of government of Cyprus.

clue.text: Maiden walked round, about to leave

indicators.note: the reversed walk goes about the maiden, surrounding it
turned round means the word is written backwards

parts.note: paced means walked with measured steps
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman walks around, about to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns PACED to DECAP, and 'about' puts M inside it; a maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly, often secretly.

clue.text: Woman taking A opposing position?

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A woman adopts a contrary point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female given name.

clue.text: De Gaulle's refusal to receive a European leader, once

indicators.note: the refusal takes in the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a French leader would say no in French, non
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: General de Gaulle refuses to meet a fellow European statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles de Gaulle famously vetoed Britain's entry to the Common Market with 'non'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was the French emperor and general of two centuries ago.

clue.text: Oscar's right for film director

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: An Academy Award is fitting for a movie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award; it is the writer Oscar Wilde. Billy Wilder directed Some Like It Hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder made Some Like It Hot and The Apartment.

clue.text: Defeat in east: nothing unusual in that?

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrashing in the east is regarded as quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standard and everyday, done regularly, holds no surprise.

clue.text: In Pennsylvania, North America, find brilliant cure for illness

indicators.note: the brilliant piece goes in among the letters of the place names

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
ace means excellent, brilliant

explanation.surface: A medical breakthrough is made somewhere in the American north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal remedy is supposed to heal every ailment.

clue.text: Quite attractive

explanation.surface: Someone is described as rather good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite: fairly, as in fairly good; attractive: good-looking, pleasing to the eye.

clue.text: Male name, one adopted by Greek actor

indicators.note: the one is taken into the family of the next pieces, so it goes inside them

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A man's name is taken on by a Greek performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Odour has spread to English pub

indicators.note: spread out means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smell drifts through to an English tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or bar beside a main road.

clue.text: Detective, say, returns instinctively to abode

indicators.note: say signals that the detective's name is spoken, with the silent L

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes, the fictional detective

explanation.surface: A detective heads straight back to his lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes is pronounced without the L, so it sounds like the verb for a pigeon returning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon finds its way back to its loft by instinct.

clue.text: Trunk must be carried by actors occasionally

indicators.note: the body part is carried inside the words that follow, held within their letters

explanation.surface: A piece of luggage has to be lugged about by players now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' looks like luggage; it is the body. 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the human body without head and limbs.

clue.text: New fitting in faulty heating machine needing lots of attention

indicators.note: the new part is fitted inside the broken machine
a faulty machine is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new part is installed in a broken boiler that demands constant care.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a person or thing that demands constant care and effort to keep happy.

clue.text: Communists, so to speak, who hit the target?

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are spoken out loud

parts.note: followers of Karl Marx are Marx men

explanation.surface: Reds, as it were, score a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpshooters are skilled at shooting and find the bull's-eye.

clue.text: African fellow joined by American briefly

parts.note: Ken is a man's name, so a fellow

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a Yank is an American

explanation.surface: A man teams up with someone from the United States for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a native of the East African country Kenya.
